chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday, it is not befitting for anyone to speak until the Imam finishes his sermon; and when the Imam finishes the two sermons, one may speak in the interval between that and the establishment of the prayer. Whether one hears the recitation or does not hear, it suffices.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during the Friday sermon and the time between the sermon and prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal ruling that speaking is prohibited during the Imam's Friday sermon but permitted in the interval before the prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on attentive listening (istima') as a condition for the validity of the khutbah. It clarifies that the listener's obligation to remain silent is tied specifically to the sermon itself, distinguishing it from the subsequent Quranic recitation which may or may not be audible depending on the mosque's acoustics and the Imam's volume.
